subtopic: Kernel availability / INT4 across GPU generations
learningObjective: Identify which GPU generations support which quantized Tensor Core precisions and what falls back to software-emulated kernels.
stem: For quantized inference kernels, which of the following are TRUE about hardware / kernel availability across NVIDIA GPU generations? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: INT8 Tensor Cores are supported on Turing (sm_75), Ampere (sm_80/86), Ada (sm_89), and Hopper (sm_90); INT8 GEMM is broadly available via cuBLAS / CUTLASS on all these.
FP8 Tensor Cores debuted on Hopper (sm_90) and Ada (sm_89); Ampere (sm_80) does NOT support FP8 Tensor Cores, and W8A8-FP8 kernels on Ampere fall back to FP16 or software emulation.

For W4A16 kernels, the INT4 weights are typically dequantized to FP16/BF16 in registers and consumed by FP16/BF16 Tensor Cores; this means W4A16 works on any GPU with FP16/BF16 Tensor Cores (Ampere+), regardless of whether that GPU has 'INT4 Tensor Core' hardware.
Because INT4 was deprecated in Hopper's Tensor Cores, W4A16 kernels are slower on H100 than on A100.
Any quantized precision that lacks a native Tensor Core kernel can still deliver speedup as long as the compiler can generate a software-emulated INT/FP kernel on CUDA cores.

explanation: A: INT8 Tensor Cores exist from Turing onward; supported by cuBLAS Lt and CUTLASS. B: FP8 debuted on Hopper (and Ada with the sm_89 subset); Ampere lacks FP8 Tensor Cores, so FP8-labeled kernels there are fallbacks. C: W4A16 kernels dequant INT4→FP16 in registers and use FP16 TCs; INT4 Tensor Core hardware is not required. D is misleading: while the H100 architecture does deprioritize dedicated INT4 Tensor Core paths that existed on Turing/Ampere, W4A16 kernels do not rely on INT4 TC and remain fast on H100 (through FP16/FP8 Tensor Cores). E is false: CUDA-core INT/FP emulation is often SLOWER than the FP16 baseline it tries to beat; 'as long as a kernel exists' is not the same as 'delivers speedup'.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: INT8 TC availability across generations.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: W4A16 uses FP16 TCs via dequant-in-register.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: W4A16 does not rely on INT4 TC.
optionExplanations.E: Wrong: fallback kernels are often slower, not faster.

assumptions: Standard NVIDIA GPU generation naming (Turing sm_75, Ampere sm_80/86, Ada sm_89, Hopper sm_90).
nonImplications: Does not imply INT8 has the same peak throughput on every generation — Hopper INT8 is faster per SM than Turing INT8.
Does not imply all frameworks expose all precisions — some may require build flags or specific runtime versions.

distractorRationales.D: Ties W4A16 speed to nonexistent INT4 TC dependence.
